title: Architecture, peinture et sculpture de la maison de ville d'Amsterdam, représentée en CIX figures en taille-douce ...
shelf_note: A 1719 French description of the Amsterdam Town Hall's plates. The image and text match that. No tradition or collection is recorded to check it against.
structure_note: Each record is a two-page opening: the OCR joins two printed pages with '---', and the image is an unsplit spread. On this record the text is printed pp. 18–19 (Planches LXXIII–LXXXIV), but the image is the next opening, pp. 20–21 (Planches LXXXV–CIII). The OCR ends with the catchword 'Chien;', and the image's p.20 begins 'Chien; c'est pourquoi le Sculpteur a placé ici un Loup'. That points to an image/text offset of one opening (I1), not a misread numeral. The 4 printed_backsteps and 2 repeats may come from this offset or from misread leaf numbers on plate pages. Only 16 of 169 records carry a printed number. The counts disagree on translation: structure pages_translated 0, but pages_translated_field 127.

missing.english: that Goddess who was the Daughter of Jupiter and Diana
missing.why: Mythology makes Venus the daughter of Dione, not of Diana. The source has the slip (or a variant) and the English repeats it without comment, a few lines after presenting Diana as a virgin huntress. A reader is left confused.

missing.english: named Saturn from a Latin word meaning *To Sow*
missing.why: The Latin word behind the etymology (serere, satum) is never given, so the pun is lost. The note gives only the French 'Semer'.

missing.english: the Chamber of the Extraordinary Aldermen
missing.why: This is a Dutch civic office (the buitengewone schepenen), and a general reader cannot tell what 'Extraordinary' means here.

book_verdict: The text and its English are a careful, faithful rendering of pp. 18–19, but this record's image is the next opening, pp. 20–21, so a reader sees a scan that does not match the text beside it. Raw <column-break/> tags also leak into the English.
